Potanthus pava.notes: Represented in peninsular India by Potanthus pava pava; its elongated forewing shape and male orange base in space 3 provide helpful visual cues in the field.

Telicota colon.headline: Bright palm-dart whose jagged orange band shoots vein teeth into the black border
Telicota colon.upperwing: Bright golden-orange and black; forewing discal band projects long orange vein-teeth outward into the black border along veins 1b-4 while spots 4-5 step outward like a staircase, and males bear a curved pale grey sex-brand set toward the inner edge of the black oblique bar; hindwing shows a bright orange band and cell spot.
Telicota colon.underwing: Bright yellow-ochre across the hindwing, where the veins crossing the golden-orange discal band are distinctly dark-dusted against a dark-spotted band border.
Telicota colon.similarSpecies: Separated from Dark Palm-Dart (Telicota bambusae) by paler bright golden-orange colour, jagged vein streaks entering the black forewing border, strongly staggered spots 4-5, and dark-dusted veins across the hindwing underside band; smaller than Plain Palm-dart (Cephrenes acalle), whose males lack a brand.
Telicota colon.habitat: Coastal palm belts, bamboo groves, paddy-edge hedges, open scrub, gardens, and foothill clearings.
Telicota colon.behavior: Powerful, territorial flier defending sunlit palm or bamboo perches; basks in crisp two-angle jet-plane posture and visits Lantana, Ixora, and damp mud.
Telicota colon.season: Common throughout the year across plains and foothills, peaking from September to January.
Telicota colon.tnDistribution: Widespread statewide from Chennai coast and Cauvery delta to Coimbatore, Salem, Eastern Ghats, and Western Ghats foothills.
Telicota colon.notes: The classic bright palm-dart of Tamil Nadu gardens and coastal coconut avenues, readily spotted by the jagged orange teeth along its outer forewing veins.

Telicota bambusae.headline: Deep tawny bamboo palm-dart with clean undarkened veins across the hindwing below
Telicota bambusae.upperwing: Rich dark brown-black marked with deeper, warmer orange-tawny bands; forewing discal band has a cleaner outer edge lacking long orange vein teeth piercing into the black border and less staggered spots 4-5, while males carry a straight dark-grey brand centered in the black oblique bar; females darker with narrower bands.
Telicota bambusae.underwing: Warm deep ochreous-olive across the hindwing, where the veins crossing the tawny discal band remain clean orange-ochre without dark dusting and the band is bordered in crisp dark brown.
Telicota bambusae.similarSpecies: Separated from Pale Palm-Dart (Telicota colon) by deeper tawny-orange tone, un-toothed outer edge of the forewing discal band, central male brand, and clean undarkened veins crossing the hindwing underside band; separated from Plain Palm-dart (Cephrenes acalle) by smaller size and male forewing brand.
Telicota bambusae.habitat: Bamboo clumps in moist forests, wooded urban parks, riparian groves, and foothill gardens.
Telicota bambusae.behavior: Swift, territorial flier active around bamboo thickets and palm fronds, especially during morning sun and late afternoon; basks in jet-plane posture and feeds at Lantana and damp ground.
Telicota bambusae.season: Active year-round in humid and bamboo-rich zones, peaking from August to January.
Telicota bambusae.tnDistribution: Widespread across Tamil Nadu hills and wooded plains including Coimbatore, Kallar, Siruvani, Mudumalai, Anamalais, Yercaud, Kolli Hills, and Chennai parks.
Telicota bambusae.notes: Frequently listed under Telicota ancilla (T. a. bambusae) in Indian checklists; larvae roll leaves of both wild forest bamboos and cultivated garden palms.

Cephrenes acalle.headline: Heavy-bodied coconut palm-dart lacking a male brand and oiled purple below in females
Cephrenes acalle.upperwing: Large, sturdy dark chocolate-brown skipper with rich tawny-orange bands; forewing bears an orange cell streak, subapical band, and broad orange discal band crossed by dark-dusted veins, with males completely lacking any sex-brand; hindwing carries a broad tawny band and cell spot, while females are much darker.
Cephrenes acalle.underwing: Rich ochreous-orange across the hindwing in males with a dark-bordered discal band, whereas females display a distinctive oily purplish-olive sheen over dark chocolate-brown with obscure band outlines.
Cephrenes acalle.similarSpecies: Noticeably larger and broader-winged than both Pale Palm-Dart (Telicota colon) and Dark Palm-Dart (Telicota bambusae), separated cleanly in males by lacking any forewing sex-brand and in females by the glossy purplish-olive hindwing underside.
Cephrenes acalle.habitat: Coconut groves, ornamental palm gardens, coastal towns, moist foothills, and shaded palm-lined avenues.
Cephrenes acalle.behavior: Fast, robust flier patrolling coconut and ornamental palm crowns; perches boldly on sunlit palm leaflets in a two-angle jet-plane stance and feeds at Ixora, Lantana, and Hibiscus flowers.
Cephrenes acalle.season: Common year-round across palm-growing plains and foothills.
Cephrenes acalle.tnDistribution: Statewide across Tamil Nadu coastal belts, Chennai, Cuddalore coast, Cauvery delta, Coimbatore, Madurai, and foothill plantations.
Cephrenes acalle.notes: Represented in South India by Cephrenes acalle oceanica; caterpillars stitch stout palm leaflets into tough shelters and are among the commonest large orange skippers in Tamil Nadu gardens.
